components.name: Compact island
components.description: Illustrative local 273 × 41pt example around the measured 185 × 33pt housing. One CSS pixel represents one native point; the count is example data and the inline symbol is a simplified preview of the native SF Symbol.

narrative.overview:
Levels uses a compact black island around the camera housing, expanding downward into native macOS audio controls. Its expression comes from the silhouette, restrained mint accents, clear app identities, and aligned levels. The confirmed direction is recorded in docs/ISLAND_DESIGN.md; platform and native-control commitments are in PRODUCT.md.

This document describes the implemented island and optional menu bar popover. SwiftUI and AppKit remain the rendering authority; the sidecar's HTML examples are illustrative translations, with one CSS pixel representing one macOS point. Window-level review covered compact, expanded, and many-app states. Full-display pixel positioning was not captured; reported NSScreen coordinates and geometry tests support placement logic only. Saved scroll captures intermittently omit layers, while the user confirmed labels and sliders remain visible on screen.

The saved Display Mode choice switches between the notch-aware island and a 400pt charcoal native popover. Both use the same audio model and retain current levels. The popover adds a header glyph, native close action, and mint activity labels.
keyCharacteristics: Black island and charcoal popover with shared mint controls and status.
System SF typography, SF Symbols, and native menus and sliders.
A camera-housing cap above interactive mixer content.
Fixed surrounding sections and a bounded, scrollable app list.

rules.name: The App Identity Rule
rules.body: Playing apps precede idle apps, with localized alphabetical ordering within each group. Rows and saved levels use stable app IDs rather than list positions; owning bundle IDs are used where available. Reordering must retain each app's values.

dos: Do derive the housing cap and gap from the current screen's reported geometry.
Do keep interactive mixer content beneath the cap and long app lists bounded.
Do place playing apps first, then idle apps, alphabetically within each group, while preserving identity and levels.
Do retain native control behavior, system typography, and monospaced percentage digits.
Do verify visible labels and sliders in the running app when saved scroll captures omit layers.
donts: Don't turn the measured housing dimensions into universal constants.
Don't draw a manual popover arrow, put one on the island, or add simulated audio meters. NSPopover owns its arrow.
Don't replace system-managed menus, controls, or shadows with invented web styling.
Don't treat window captures or geometry tests as proof of full-display pixel alignment or untested hardware behavior.
